item.title: LiveLoRA: Exact KV Cache Migration Across LoRA Updates for LLM Agents
item.description:
LiveLora lets you upgrade an LLM adapter without re-running the whole chat history, saving time and storage. It freezes early decoder layers and keeps KV cache entries consistent across adapter updates, giving almost 69× speedups over full-history re-prefill on large sessions.

IT Breakdown: If you manage LLM-serving, update your deployment pipeline to keep the first decoder blocks frozen and enable LiveLora’s cache migration logic: 1) Freeze lower blocks and adapter down-projections. 2) During a new adapter release, migrate existing KV cache entries to the new format and recompute the final token. 3) Commit the updated cache and logits before serving next token. This reduces re‑prefill costs and storage for long-running sessions.

item.title: Decoupling Solving from Abstention: Single-Rollout Conformal Risk Control for Hard-Budget LLM Reasoning
item.description:
Hard token limits stop LLMs before answering, risking wrong outputs. The authors built Tail-CRC, a single‑rollout method that first trains a solver to respect token budgets, then uses conformal risk control to decide whether to submit the answer. It boosts correct‑submission rates by 15–30 points, cuts wrong answers to under 7%, and saves 4–13% inference cost.

IT Breakdown: If you manage LLM inference with token budgets, use Tail‑CRC: 1) fine‑tune your model to stop at the budget with a binary reward; 2) freeze the model and add a conformal risk‑control layer that checks token‑log‑probability surprise; 3) deploy the single‑rollout pipeline and tune the risk target to keep wrong‑submission rates below your desired threshold.

item.title: TideSand: Performance-Accurate Sandbox Multiplexing for LLM Agents
item.description:
TideSand is a sandbox system that smartly shares CPU and memory across multiple large‑language‑model agents. It schedules tool calls, swaps out idle memory, and rolls back only when needed, giving up to 10× more throughput and up to 44% better call accuracy compared with simple reservation or overcommit approaches.

IT Breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure, here is what to do: 1) evaluate whether your LLM workloads hit CPU or memory contention; 2) if so, test TideSand’s agent‑aware scheduling and speculative swapping on a small set of models; 3) integrate the sandbox layer before deploying agents to improve throughput and reliability.

item.title: TowerBridge: Bridging the Dual-Encoder Modality Gap via Weight-Space Programming
item.description:
The paper solves the problem of a modality gap that hurts image‑text retrieval in CLIP‑style models. Researchers built TowerBridge, a quick, model‑agnostic recipe that tweaks weights based on a statistic to close the gap without hurting performance. It improves retrieval scores by up to 17 points on COCO and 6.6 on Flickr30k across many checkpoints, while keeping inference costs the same.

IT Breakdown: If you manage dual‑encoder models, use TowerBridge: step 1 – run the provided script on 25,000 labelled pairs to compute the statistic; step 2 – apply the closed‑form weight edits to your encoder weights; step 3 – test retrieval and hubness – you should see a boost without extra inference cost.

item.title: [News] Stalwart is now a drop-in replacement for Microsoft Exchange
item.description: Stalwart 1.2.0 has been released as a fully compatible, open‑source drop‑in replacement for Microsoft Exchange, supporting MAPI‑HTTP, EWS, Exchange ActiveSync, and Autodiscover. It enables Outlook, Apple Mail, and mobile clients to connect seamlessly without needing a Microsoft Exchange server.

item.title: [News] OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
item.description: OpenAI and Cisco have launched Shirudo, an open‑source runtime that lets operators protect running Linux systems with AI‑generated eBPF shields while patches are pending. The tool can block exploits like Java4Shell in real time without restarting services, using cryptographic verification and TPM support.

item.title: [News] How to tell a cyberattack from a plain old outage
item.description: Microsoft Exchange and other critical services suffered widespread outages this week, prompting debate over whether these incidents were cyberattacks or operational failures. Cloudflare’s CEO clarified that most such events stem from system complexity rather than malicious intent.

item.title: [News] Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
item.description: Anthropic has launched Claude Ship, a new suite of AI agents that can review, fix, and automatically approve code changes based on team‑defined policies. The tool adds an automated approval layer to the GitHub pull‑request workflow, potentially speeding up the release cycle for teams that rely heavily on CI/CD pipelines.

item.title: [News] Anthropic Created a Honeypot to Lure AI Agents Into Misbehaving
item.description: Anthropic has released Siren, a honeypot test that lures AI agents into misbehaving within simulated sandboxes to evaluate their propensity for exploiting zero‑day vulnerabilities. This research underscores the growing risk that advanced agents could bypass security boundaries, potentially impacting any organization that deploys AI‑powered tools.
